dual_master_analysis.today: NO dual-master condition arises from populating R45/R47/R49. On SDA and SCL both resistors bridge the identical net pair, so fitting both puts 0R in parallel with 10k between the same two nets - electrically no change. The hazard the contract guards cannot occur today because only ONE master (U9-ESP) is wired to the shared bus at all, and the RT1062 is on no I2C bus. The safety property is VACUOUSLY satisfied, which is worse than a violation: it is satisfied by the absence of the configuration the contract requires.
dual_master_analysis.latent: The hazard ARMS the moment the correct per-owner split is built. If A3-RT-DEBUG assigns RT I2C balls and MOTION_SDA is split into RT_I2C_SDA via R44 and S3_I2C_SDA via R45, and R45 is still populated, MOTION_SDA is tied to BOTH masters simultaneously - the uncontrolled dual-master connection contracts/motion-interface.md exists to prevent. So the fake DNP must be fixed BEFORE or WITH the split, never after.
dual_master_analysis.int_is_not_a_dual_master_risk: MOTION_INT1 is a single push-pull OUTPUT from U13-MOT feeding MCU INPUTS. Driving it into two receivers is electrically fine - one driver, two loads, no contention. The XOR on INT is about which MCU services the interrupt in firmware, not about electrical contention. Do not conflate it with the SDA/SCL hazard.
dual_master_analysis.value_class_is_also_wrong: A 10k in series on an I2C line does not select an owner - it forms a resistive divider against the 4.7k bus pull-ups and neither side would meet V_OL. If R45/R47 are ever intended as a fitted alternative they must be 0R, like their R44/R46 counterparts. As drawn they are wrong on exclusion status AND wrong on value class for the position they occupy.

fit_side_is_correct.measured: R44/R46/R48-MOT bind device 0f3d5fb5eae54546a764946f2555ccb3, an 11-member family whose only Name value is '0R', with Supplier Part RC0402FR-070RL.1 - a genuine 0 ohm. The FIT side is a real 0R link.
fit_side_is_correct.conclusion: The concern that the fitted side might also be a 10k is NOT borne out. Only the DNP side is mis-specified.

MOTION_INT1.measured: genuine per-owner nets exist. MOTION_INT_RT reaches U6-RTC ball L11. MOTION_INT_S3 binds one pin; its second labelled stub (wire e8944, segment [4170,4365,4040,4365]) is drawn in the ESP block but lands on no pin, nearest U9-ESP pin 90 units away.

rt1062_i2c_presence.measured: U6-RTC binds 41 distinct nets across both symbol parts (e3295, e3673). None is an I2C net. There is no RT_I2C_SDA or RT_I2C_SCL anywhere in the frozen source.
rt1062_i2c_presence.consequence: contracts/motion-interface.md names RT1062 as the default motion owner, but the RT1062 has no data path to U13-MOT. It sees MOTION_INT_RT only. The ownership matrix cannot be repaired by fixing resistors - the RT leg does not exist to select.
rt1062_i2c_presence.blocking_dependency: A3-RT-DEBUG must assign two RT1062 balls to RT_I2C_SDA / RT_I2C_SCL before this block can be built into a real XOR.

motion_pullups.measured: R50-MOT 4.7k pulls up MOTION_SDA. No pull-up exists on MOTION_SCL. With the 0R links fitted the shared-bus pull-ups (R4-PWR1, R28-AUD, R29-AUD, all 4.7k) serve both lines, so the bus works today.
motion_pullups.risk: The moment the buses are genuinely split per owner, SCL has no pull-up on the sensor side. Fix it in the same edit as the split.

led_ownership.verdict: PASS - contracts/led-interface.md output_owner RT1062 is satisfied for both channels; U9-ESP touches no LED net.

level_shift.evidence: TI datasheet: single bus buffer gate/line driver with 3-state output; when OE# is low, true data is passed from the A input to the Y output. Function table: OE# H gives Hi-Z. LCSC parametric Channel Type = Unidirectional.
level_shift.vih_at_5v: 2.0 V min across the whole VCC range, so a 3.3 V CMOS high is a valid TTL high
level_shift.vcc_range: 4.5 V to 5.5 V - LED-rail droop below 4.5 V puts the shifter out of spec (VAL-G3 copper-sizing concern)
level_shift.pinout_match: schematic symbol matches the DBV package exactly: 1=OE#, 2=A, 3=GND, 4=Y, 5=VCC
level_shift.verdict: PASS - deterministic and unidirectional, not a bidirectional autosensing part.

boot_state.measured: LED_OE_L binds exactly two pins (U14-LED.1, R53-LED.1) and LED_OE_R binds exactly two (U15-LED.1, R54-LED.1). R53/R54 are 10k to GND. No controller reaches either OE# pin.
boot_state.consequence: OE# is hard-tied low, so per the TI function table both buffers are enabled from the instant +5V_LED_L/R is valid and Y follows A unconditionally. The A inputs come from RT1062 pads GPIO_B0_00 and GPIO_B0_01. At cold power-on and throughout RT1062 reset, before firmware configures those pads, nothing in this circuit holds the buffer inputs or the 5 V strip data lines at a defined level. No pull-down exists on LED_D0_3V3/LED_D1_3V3 or on LED_D0_J/LED_D1_J, and firmware has no way to force the outputs Hi-Z.
boot_state.note: TI recommended operating conditions note 3 - all unused inputs must be held at VCC or GND - is the same rule applied to a pad that is not yet driven.
bounded_repair_options: A (RECOMMENDED): 10k pull-down from LED_D0_3V3 to GND and from LED_D1_3V3 to GND. Two 0402 parts, holds both outputs at a defined 0 V through power-on and reset, costs no RT pads and no firmware sequencing.

B: flip R53/R54 to pull OE# UP to +5V_LED_L/R and route LED_OE_L/LED_OE_R to two RT1062 pads. Outputs boot Hi-Z and firmware enables them. Costs two RT pads and STILL needs a pull-down at J2/J3 to define the strip line while Hi-Z, so it adds to option A rather than replacing it.
Add B on top of A only if a firmware-commanded LED blackout is wanted for thermal or fault response.

thermal_feedback.measured: LED_THERM_L binds exactly two pins - RT1-LED.1 and U6-RTC ball L12 (GPIO_AD_B1_04). LED_THERM_R binds RT2-LED.1 and U6-RTC ball K12 (GPIO_AD_B1_05). RT1/RT2 are NCP15XH103F03RC 10k NTCs with their other terminal on GND.
thermal_feedback.defect: No bias resistor exists from 3V3 to either LED_THERM net, so no divider exists. An NTC with one end on GND and the other on an ADC input has no excitation - the ADC reads an undriven node, not a temperature. Both thermal-feedback channels are unreadable as drawn, and the failure is silent: firmware receives a plausible-looking ADC number that means nothing.
thermal_feedback.bounded_repair: Add one bias resistor per channel from 3V3 to LED_THERM_L and LED_THERM_R. 10k is the conventional match to a 10k-at-25C NTC, but the value should place the NTC mid-span across the intended monitoring range and belongs to the thermal lane (D15). This audit asserts only that the resistor must exist.

branch_protection.topology: 5V_SYS -> U4-PWR2 (TPS259474L eFuse, single device) -> 5V_LED_COMMON (C11-PWR2 22uF) -> FB1-PWR2 / FB2-PWR2 (BLM21PG221SN1D, 220 ohm at 100 MHz ferrites) -> +5V_LED_L / +5V_LED_R
branch_protection.reasoning: The only element between the common node and each branch is a ferrite bead. A ferrite is an EMI element, not a protection device and not a switch. A short on one strip pulls the shared eFuse down and takes both channels out, and neither channel can be independently powered down for thermal response, fault isolation or bring-up.
branch_protection.fault_visibility: U4-PWR2 pins 3 (PG/AUXOFF) and 4 (PGTH/FLT#) carry No-Connect flags and pin 10 (ITIMER) is also No-Connect. The TI datasheet characterises the device with AUXOFF/FLT/PGTH/PG all open and an open ITIMER simply gives minimum overcurrent blanking, so these are legitimate INTENTIONAL_NC, not defects.
branch_protection.latching_hazard: The fitted part is the L suffix - latched off. EN/UVLO is hard-tied to 5V_SYS and FLT# is not connected, so a latched LED overcurrent trip cannot be cleared by firmware, requires a full input power cycle, and gives firmware no signal to explain why the strips went dark. With ITIMER open the blanking interval is minimum, so a strip hot-plug inrush is the most likely route into that state.
branch_protection.current_limit: ~0.96 A, DETERMINED. TI: I_ILM = 3334 / R_ILM(ohm). R8-PWR2 orders as Supplier Part C185418 / MPN RC0402FR-073K48L - a genuine 3.48k matching its drawn value, giving 0.96 A, inside the recommended R_ILM range of 549 R to 6.65 k.
branch_protection.correction_2026_08_28: An earlier revision of this audit called the limit UNDETERMINED because R8-PWR2 supplierId reads RC0402FR-0710KL.1 (10k). That was wrong: supplierId is a stale library-inherited string on several parts, and the orderable identity is the Supplier Part field. Re-read field by field from bom_flat.csv.
branch_protection.soft_start: C68-PWR2 2.2 nF gives SR = 2000/2200 = 0.91 V/ms, so the rail ramps in about 5.5 ms.
branch_protection.ownership: A2-RAILS owns the device choice. This lane's finding is only that ferrite beads do not satisfy branch protection or branch enable, and that FLT# should reach an RT1062 input if a trip is to be observable.

series_data_resistors.measured: R51-LED and R52-LED are RC0402FR-0733RL, 33 ohm, in series between each buffer output and its connector data pin.
series_data_resistors.requirement: The footprint is justified - it damps the fast AHCT edge into an unterminated strip lead. The VALUE is transmission-line dependent, a function of driver output impedance and routed trace and lead geometry, none of which exists yet. 33 ohm is a donor-circuit number and must be released to TUNE_TBD in both the BOM and the schematic value field, then set at VAL-G3.

branch_bypass_candidate.status: CANDIDATE ONLY - not fitted, not a schematic requirement, not added by this audit

correct_topology.root_cause: The 0R/DNP pair is on the wrong side of the bus. A link between MOTION_SDA and the shared bus isolates the SENSOR, not the MASTER. Owner selection is a property of which master is attached, so the pair must sit on each master leg. No arrangement of R44-R49 in their present positions can produce a real XOR.

bus_census.note: One bus, four slaves, exactly one master-capable device.

correct_topology.required_shape: U2-PWR1 + U11-AUD + U12-NFC + U13-MOT permanently on I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL (bus pull-ups here); then I2C_SDA -> 0R FIT -> RT_I2C_SDA (RT1062, default owner) and I2C_SDA -> 0R DNP -> S3_I2C_SDA (ESP32-S3). Same for SCL. Two resistor pairs total, four parts, on the MASTER legs - not three pairs on the sensor leg.
consequences: R44/R45 and R46/R47 move from the sensor leg to the master legs, or are deleted and replaced there. In their present positions they are not owner-selection hardware.
MOTION_SDA / MOTION_SCL collapse into I2C_SDA / I2C_SCL - the sensor is a slave and has no reason to sit behind a link.

MOTION_INT1 keeps its _RT/_S3 split through R48/R49. The interrupt is the one signal whose XOR is already correctly placed, because an interrupt line genuinely is point-to-point between sensor and owner. Follow it as the model for the master legs, not for the bus legs.

Recompute the pull-up budget in the same edit: once MOTION_SDA merges into I2C_SDA, R50-MOT 4.7k lands in parallel with R4-PWR1 and R28-AUD giving about 1.57k on SDA against 2.35k on SCL - asymmetric and stronger than intended. Consolidate to one pull-up pair on the shared bus.
All four matrix parts must be 0 ohm, with the DNP half excluded via 'Add into BOM'='no' rather than by a Name field.

isolation_verdict.reasoning: Yes, and more easily than the question assumed - there is only one master socket to arbitrate. NFC, audio and the power monitor are slaves and do not care which master is talking; their presence does not force a dual-master condition.
ruled_out: Duplicating the bus per owner with its own copy of the slaves - impossible, the slaves are single instances.

Leaving both masters permanently attached and arbitrating in firmware - legal I2C multi-master, but it needs both masters powered and both stacks implementing arbitration, and on a validation platform testing one owner at a time it is exactly the uncontrolled dual-master connection the contract forbids.
Selecting on the sensor leg - what is drawn today; it isolates the wrong device.
isolation_verdict.blocking_dependency: A3-RT-DEBUG must assign two RT1062 balls to RT_I2C_SDA / RT_I2C_SCL. Until then there is no RT master leg to link to and the matrix cannot be built in any position.

drc_1458_delta.confirmed: Five of this audit's six U13-MOT findings are re-confirmed by netlist-grade evidence on a state NEWER than the frozen source: CS, SDO/SA0, RES and both spare GND pins are still floating. None is a registration artefact.
drc_1458_delta.mechanism: 95 pins resolved in one sweep across 17 designators spanning every functional block (U6-RTC 31, U9-ESP 19, U12-NFC 10, plus connectors and switches). The mutation ledger names it - STATE_QUARANTINED reason: 'Captain applied unused-pin NC crosses after the open NFC NC transaction'. These pins were DECLARED, not connected.
drc_1458_delta.inference_warning: U9-ESP reaching zero floating pins is NOT evidence that any S3-side net became terminated. A No-Connect cross asserts a pin is deliberately unused - the opposite of a connection. No finding depending on MOTION_INT_S3 being unterminated is weakened by it; the last direct measurement puts MOTION_INT_S3 at one bound pin, and an NC sweep cannot add one.
drc_1458_delta.sharper_risk: If an NC cross was applied to the S3 pin meant to receive MOTION_INT_S3, the S3 owner leg is now documented as permanently unused - worse than unterminated, because it reads as intentional.
drc_1458_delta.drc_rule_caveat: The DRC 'single network' warning is NOT a reliable dangling-net detector: MOTION_INT_S3 was a one-pin net in the frozen source and appeared in neither run's list, while BUCK_PG did. Its silence is not evidence.
drc_1458_delta.regression: U3-PWR2.5 became floating between the two runs - outside this lane.

cross_lane_handoffs.item: Confirm against live whether the 14:58 NC sweep placed a No-Connect cross on the ESP32-S3 pin that was meant to receive MOTION_INT_S3. If it did, the S3 owner leg is now documented as permanently unused.
U3-PWR2.5 became floating between the 12:17 and 14:58 DRC runs - a regression outside this lane.

R45/R47/R49-MOT carry Name='DNP' and a fabricated Manufacturer Part 'RC0402FR-07DNP', but their orderable Supplier Part is 'RC0402FR-0710KL.1' - a real 10k - and they carry NO 'Add into BOM'='no' attribute. Re-derived from source: that attribute exists and works on C43-ESP, C44-ESP and C52-AUD, and is absent on all three MOT resistors. As shipped they will be populated as 10k.

The same fake-DNP pattern (Name='DNP', MPN 'RC0402FR-07DNP', orderable 10k, no 'Add into BOM'='no') appears on exactly seven resistors board-wide: R40-AUD, R41-AUD, R45-MOT, R47-MOT, R49-MOT, R56-VAL, R57-VAL. Re-derived independently by scanning drawn Name against orderable Supplier Part across all 65 RC0402 resistors; no other resistor mismatches once notation differences (5.1k vs 5K1, 32.4k vs 32K4, 1.05M vs 1M05) are discounted.

WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28. R8-PWR2 orders as C185418 / RC0402FR-073K48L, a genuine 3.48k, so the LED-branch eFuse current limit is a determined 0.96 A. The earlier UNDETERMINED claim misread the stale supplierId field instead of Supplier Part.

U4-PWR2 is a TPS259474L - the LATCHED variant. Its FLT#/PG (pins 3,4) and ITIMER (pin 10) are No-Connect, and EN/UVLO is hard-tied to 5V_SYS. A latched LED overcurrent trip therefore requires a full power cycle to clear and is invisible to firmware.

The shared I2C bus lands on U9-ESP pins 36/37, whose symbol names are RXD0/TXD0 - the ESP32-S3 ROM bootloader console pins. U9-ESP has only five nets in the frozen source (GND, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL, ESP_UART0_RX, ESP_UART0_TX) and no supply net.
U6-RTC touches no I2C net at all. Whatever RT1062 balls are chosen for RT_I2C_SDA/SCL must come from this lane.

val_g3_requirements.text: Mount U13-MOT on a rigid structural section near the assembled structural centre - not on a board edge, connector tongue or unsupported cantilever.
val_g3_requirements.action: RECORDED ONLY - not acted on at VAL-G2

val_g3_requirements.text: R51/R52-LED series data resistor values are transmission-line dependent and must be set from the routed geometry, not inherited from a donor circuit.
